searchText: Glacier Hardforks don't happen often, right? A one-time ping is not something super bad Worst thing here is that the hardfork announcement is there along with... consensus/execution specs release announcements, and random server-related announcements :/ Anyway, I am not a hardfork coordinator so not really my job. Just my two cents. <@!354681205842771973> we email all miners directly and reach out to a bunch of infrastructure providers as well. A lot of different people are in this server for different reasons so I'm weary of `@everyone`'ing people when it's not an emergency. If we had to fork on a very short notice, we'd probably do it! > we email all miners directly and reach out to a bunch of infrastructure providers as well. But not all infrastructure providers... And miners probably too. Anyway, not here to argue about this. Right, but the "main" way people find out is via the blog.ethereum.org posts 🙂 That said, if you have other channels you think we should post this in, I'm definitely open to doing so! Well, if we look long term the best thing we can do is to have an endpoint that returns the minimum versions for different clients in order to support the upcoming hardfork, and make all clients polling that endpoint once a minute and notify the user if they need to upgrade the node with the ERROR log level Given that hardforks are pretty common on Ethereum, this would help a lot. <timbeiko> Oh, neat idea! <@!97774605351010304> I think I found a small "bug" in the tracker: OE _does_ have a release, but it's in a weird state right now. We added this to the AG blog post: > Note: OpenEthereum, which was announced as deprecated earlier this year, has released support for Arrow Glacier under version number 3.3.0-rc.14, which you can download here. The crawler counts ~300 OE nodes right now, but I wonder how many are actually good 👋 was told by peter that he can't track rc releases unfortunately :/ Ah, fair enough! Good feedback to pass back to the OE team, thanks which services still use OE? As per their Github, 3.3.0 is AG-compatible: https://github.com/openethereum/openethereum/releases/tag/v3.3.0 <https://ethernodes.org/client/openethereum> then it's looking good and we just dont track it on /arrow_glacier I'd like to answer "none" but I know that's not the case 😅 . Not sure exactly! Crazypool 😂😂😂 joking, I think some people use oe to monitor mempool and a few other things
